'''''Crepis bursifolia''''', commonly known as '''Italian hawksbeard''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Asteraceae]].<ref name=nickaeila/> It is native to southern Europe (Spain, France, Italy, Malta, Greece), as well as being sparingly naturalized in [[California]] (primarily in the hills east of [[San Francisco Bay]], but with a few collections from open spots in urban areas inside the Cities of [[Oakland, California|Oakland]] and [[San Francisco]]).<ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=crepis+bursifolia Altervista Flora Italiana, Radicchiella italiana, ''Crepis bursifolia'' L.] includes photos and European distribution map</ref><ref>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=2416 Calflora taxon report, University of California, ''Crepis bursifolia'' L., Italian hawksbeard ]</ref><ref>[http://www.maltawildplants.com/ASTR/Crepis_bursifolia.php Malta Wild Plants] in English with photos</ref>

''Crepis bursifolia''  is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] herb up to 35 cm (14 inches) tall. One plant can produce as many as 10 [[flower heads]], each with up to 60 yellow [[ray florets]] but no [[disc floret]]s.<ref name=nickaeila>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250066443 Flora of North America, Italian hawksbit, ''Crepis bursifolia'' Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 2: 805. 1753. ]</ref>
